text:
Alex Killorn is 37, has two Stanley Cup rings from Tampa, and is now a penalty-killing depth veteran on a Ducks team that suddenly can't stop winning. His own scoring has gone quiet: one goal and three points in his last ten games, two goals and six points in 18 overall, at about 16:30 a night.

Some of that is luck. He's scoring on 8% of his shots against a typical 12% for him, and the team has scored 4.4 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice. Our range for the rest of his season centres on about 33 points, which would be a normal Killorn year. The worry is the other end: the players he most resembles statistically share a habit of chances piling up against them, and his top speed sits in the bottom quarter of the league. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 0.7 wins last season, almost all of it from even-strength offense. If the bounces even out, he's useful. If they don't, his minutes are the ones a young Duck takes next.
